description: Source code for a memory technology device (MTD) manipulation tool, including functions for opening, checking, erasing, writing, verifying, and managing MTD devices, as well as command-line interface handling.

methods.name: main
methods.description: Main function handling command-line arguments and executing MTD operations based on user commands.

methods.name: mtd_open
methods.description: Opens an MTD device, trying to resolve device number from /proc/mtd if possible.

methods.name: mtd_check_open
methods.description: Checks and retrieves information about an MTD device, setting global variables for size and type.

methods.name: mtd_block_is_bad
methods.description: Checks if a specific block in the MTD device is marked as bad.

methods.name: mtd_erase_block
methods.description: Erases a specific block in the MTD device.

methods.name: mtd_write_buffer
methods.description: Writes a buffer to the MTD device at a specified offset.

methods.name: image_check
methods.description: Checks the magic number of an image file to determine its format and validity.

methods.name: mtd_check
methods.description: Checks if an MTD device can be opened and accessed.

methods.name: mtd_unlock
methods.description: Unlocks the specified MTD device or partition.

methods.name: mtd_erase
methods.description: Erases the entire MTD device or specified partitions.

methods.name: mtd_dump
methods.description: Outputs the contents of an MTD device or partition to stdout.

methods.name: mtd_verify
methods.description: Verifies the content of an MTD device against a given file by comparing MD5 hashes.

methods.name: indicate_writing
methods.description: Displays a message indicating data is being written to an MTD device.

methods.name: mtd_write
methods.description: Writes an image file to an MTD device, handling partitioning, bad blocks, and optional FIS layout updates.

methods.name: usage
methods.description: Displays usage information and command options for the tool.

methods.name: do_reboot
methods.description: Reboots the system, first via system call, then via syscall if needed.
